results.title: 10 Useful Apps And Gadgets That Can Replace Doomscrolling
results.content:
## Foqos

A screenshot of the Foqos iOS app.  Foqos/Apple

While Switchly is a great app blocker if you have an Android, it's not available on iOS. For iPhones, Foqos is the next best thing. This app is another great alternative to Brick; it's free, open-source, and doesn't feature any ads. Similar to other app blockers, you select a list of apps to block, but to unlock those apps, you need to either tap your phone against an NFC chip or scan a QR code. If you want to go the physical route, you'll need to buy your own NFC tags and tap your phone against it to set up the NFC feature. [...] The Brick Phone Lock is a small physical device that features an NFC chip. Paired with an app, it can lock certain apps on your phone. You lock these selected apps by physically tapping your phone against the Brick, and unlocking requires the same action. This creates an obvious physical barrier, as you need to be close to the Brick to unlock apps. When you tap one of these blocked apps, you'll be greeted by a screen that tells you to tap the Brick to unlock the app. You can still use an "emergency Unbrick" feature to get to the app, but you only get five of these; once you're out, there's no way to regain emergency Unbricks. [...] Switchly is a free, open-source Android app that can either work as a simple app blocker or as a much more comprehensive anti-doomscrolling tool. Like other similar apps, Switchly lets you block selected apps, but it also lets you block only selected sections in supported apps. For example, on Instagram, you can configure it to block reels, stories, and even the Explore page, leaving DMs open. While the app can set timers for social media apps, you can build schedules or even set it up so that opening an app requires tapping a physical NFC tag first. You can also set a requirement where you have to scan a QR code to unlock certain apps or app features.

results.title: What to Do Instead of Doomscrolling: 25 Simple Alternatives - Nibble Blog
results.content:
1. Pick one swap, not 25. The biggest mistake is treating this like a full routine overhaul. It's not. Choose the one alternative that sounds appealing and use it the next time you reach for your phone out of habit.Many people fail because they try to quit scrolling without finding a replacement, and bite-sized learning apps are one of the most accessible and successful alternatives to doomscrolling — just as easy to open as a social media app.
2. Replace the trigger, not just the behavior. If notifications are pulling you back into social media, turn them off. Replace them with a reminder that signals your new habit — a Nibble lesson, a podcast, or a quick breathing exercise. You're not giving anything up; you're redirecting. [...] Small, consistent swaps improve your productivity and support your mental health by reducing the low-grade stress that accumulates from hours of passive, algorithm-driven consumption

✨Ready to maximize your learning? Discover how to learn faster and better.

## Stop scrolling, start growing

Doomscrolling is a pattern that wastes your time, drains your energy, and usually leaves you worse off than when you started. Breaking free from it is about making the switch to something more rewarding, engaging, and productive.

Whether you're looking for what to do instead of scrolling, searching for things to do instead of doomscrolling, or trying to build a healthier relationship with your phone, the key is replacing the habit with something equally rewarding. [...] Social media platforms run on variable reward schedules. The algorithms powering TikTok, Instagram, and similar platforms are optimized for your attention, not your well-being. It's the same mechanism behind slot machines. Every refresh might deliver something shocking, funny, or infuriating. Your dopamine system treats that unpredictability as exciting. That's why the scroll keeps going even when you'd rather stop.

✨Knowing the techniques to stop doomscrolling makes it much easier to redirect.

## Why we doomscroll: The psychology behind the scrolling habit

There are a few key reasons why we get stuck in this pattern:
